name: Shoprite Holdings
aliases: Shoprite;Shoprite Checkers;Shoprite Group;The Shoprite Group of Companies;Shoprite Checkers Group
evidence: Shoprite Holdings' own group page describes the group's operations, and the register's own name for the company is Shoprite Holdings.
note_append: The contact roster writes this employer as Shoprite, Shoprite Checkers Group, Shoprite Financial Services, ShopriteX and The Shoprite Group of Companies. All are the one listed group and are recorded as aliases, so the 64 people on the bare 'Shoprite' spelling appear under the company instead of on an unclaimed employer string. Shoprite Financial Services and ShopriteX are divisions of the group, not separate companies, and are aliased here rather than given their own records. If either is later shown to be a separate legal entity it should become its own record with a corporate relationship.

name: PwC South Africa
evidence: PwC's South African site publishes at pwc.co.za and brands the firm as PwC, and the record's legal name is PricewaterhouseCoopers Inc.
note_append: The roster's bare 'PwC' spelling is an alias of the one South African firm, not a second employer. 25 people sat on it while 84 sat on 'PwC South Africa', which made one firm look like two. The firm's legal name is already recorded as PricewaterhouseCoopers Inc.

name: KPMG South Africa
evidence: KPMG's South African practice publishes on kpmg.com/za and names itself KPMG South Africa.
note_append: The roster's bare 'KPMG' spelling is an alias of KPMG South Africa. 4 people sat on it while 23 sat on the longer spelling; they are the same practice.

name: NTT DATA
aliases: NTT;NTT Data;NTT DATA Middle East and Africa
evidence: NTT DATA's own group site presents the business as NTT DATA, and the roster's 'NTT' and 'NTT DATA Middle East and Africa' are its regional and abbreviated spellings.
note_append: The roster uses 'NTT DATA', 'NTT' and 'NTT DATA Middle East and Africa' for the same people. The Middle East and Africa region is part of the same business rather than a separately registered South African company on the evidence read so far, so it is aliased rather than given its own record. No parent relationship is asserted beyond the name.

name: Tronox Namakwa Sands
evidence: Tronox's own site describes its Namakwa Sands operation in South Africa, and Tronox is the group whose name the roster's bare 'Tronox' spelling carries.
note_append: The roster's bare 'Tronox' spelling resolves to the Namakwa Sands record rather than to a separate company, because that is the only South African Tronox operation in the register and leaving 2 people on an unclaimed string tells a recruiter nothing. This is a judgement, not a sourced fact: if a second South African Tronox operation is later recorded, the bare spelling must be split and this alias removed.

name: Mulilo Energy
evidence: Mulilo's own site states that Mulilo is a renewable energy developer and independent power producer developing, owning and operating utility-scale solar, wind and battery energy storage in South Africa.
note_append: The website was corrected from a LinkedIn company page to mulilo.com, the company's own domain. The roster's bare 'Mulilo' is an alias. Mulilo's own page also states that Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners acquired a majority shareholding in 2023, which is recorded here as an ownership fact rather than as a corporate relationship entry, because no subsidiary structure is being claimed.
